solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's enumeration wrong at 3 down, recounted from the answer here

clue.text: Bridge-building initially is hard work for man

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word Bridge-building

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A sweeping claim that building bridges is hard labour for a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' here is a chess piece, not a person: the clue's surface hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess every piece is called a man, and a diagonal-moving piece with a mitre is one of them.

clue.text: Motorcyclist repressing constant row

indicators.note: repressing means holding something down within, so the motorcyclist word encloses the constant

parts.note: a biker rides a motorcycle
C is the standard symbol for a constant, e.g. the speed of light

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist keeps a lid on an ongoing quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a noisy squabble, and to squabble pettily is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Teacher largely uplifted, with place at public school for dunce

indicators.note: uplifted in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards
largely means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Miss is how pupils address a female teacher
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
Eton is the famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A teacher, much cheered, secures a dull pupil a place at a top school.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow-witted person, the same thing as a fool or halfwit.

clue.text: Tubby going round in these boots

indicators.note: going round means the run of letters turns about, read in the opposite direction
in signals that the letters sit inside the words these boots

explanation.surface: Someone stout walking about in these particular boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubby is a jokey synonym for fat or overweight.

clue.text: TV's Catholic priest, converted to Judaism, went on and on

indicators.note: converted to Judaism swaps the Christian title of the priest for the Jewish religious teacher's title

parts.note: Father Ted is the Irish priest in the sitcom of that name

explanation.surface: A TV priest changes religion, then can't stop talking about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is a 1990s Channel 4 sitcom about a hapless Irish priest; his title Father becomes RABBI.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk at length and tediously is informal British slang built on the animal that never stops nibbling.

clue.text: Internal CIA manoeuvres to entrap local Democrat?

indicators.note: to entrap means the shuffled letters close around the pub word
manoeuvres means the letters of Internal CIA are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the local is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub

explanation.surface: An internal CIA operation designed to ensnare a local Democratic politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is not an adjective but British slang for the neighbourhood pub. The question mark flags that a US Democrat is only one example of someone opposed to the rival party.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat in the US party sense opposes the rival party, so is, by example, against that side.

clue.text: Barking — mostly Irish area in part of London

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: barking (mad) is British slang for crazy, as is batty
Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: Barking, mostly Irish, presented as a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is itself a London district, which tempts the solver to treat it as geography; it means crazy. Battersea is a district of south-west London, home of the famous dogs' home.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a district on the south bank of the Thames, so it is a part of the capital.

clue.text: Played? Birmingham's neither won nor lost reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, here in a Birmingham accent

parts.note: a drawn match is tied; spoken in a Brummie accent the vowel shifts

explanation.surface: A sports report on Birmingham drawing its game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Birmingham (Brummie) accent famously turns the 'eye' sound into 'oy', so the result word comes out as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with something is to play with it idly; the question mark covers the sporting misdirection.

clue.text: Like fop with yen to be cuddled by attractive female

indicators.note: to be cuddled by means the first pieces are held inside the word for an attractive woman

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
and means with, as both join things together
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A foppish man with a longing wants a beautiful woman to hug him.
explanation.definitionFit: A fop is a vain, over-dressed man, also called a dandy, so the adjective describes such style.

clue.text: During recess Tory big noise reveals another put-up job

indicators.note: During means the Tory word goes within the recess word

parts.note: a recess is a break or rest
CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a ruction is a noisy disturbance or uproar

explanation.surface: A Tory bigwig, during the parliamentary recess, reveals a stitch-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big noise' reads as an important person but means an uproar; 'put-up job' looks like a fraud but means something built again.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebuilding something is literally putting it up once more, so the phrase works as a cryptic paraphrase.

clue.text: Manage to recruit Medoc's chief wine expert

indicators.note: to recruit means taking in a new member, so the manage word encloses the letter

parts.note: to cope is to manage

indicators.note: chief means the leading letter of Medoc's

parts.note: tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A wine expert manages to take on a top Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capable and skilled is close to being an expert, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Model railway in fashion

indicators.note: in means the railway abbreviation goes inside the fashion word

parts.note: the ton is an old word for high fashion

explanation.surface: A model railway that is currently fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: To model clothes is to put them on to see how they look, the phrase meaning test-wearing.

clue.text: Swimmer's extremely excitable, approaching lake

definitions.note: read as swimmer is, a creature that swims

indicators.note: extremely means the two extreme letters of excitable

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A swimmer is highly excitable as they approach the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A long snake-like fish is an obvious creature that swims.

clue.text: English cornfield after ploughing will need years to become green

indicators.note: after ploughing means the field's letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A ploughed English field will take years to recover environmentally.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the political sense means environmentally conscious and kind to nature.

clue.text: Inactivity of the secret police

definitions.meaning: inactivity means a state of stagnation or standstill
the Stasi were East Germany's secret police, so this is their possessive

explanation.surface: The sluggishness of a secret police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation, a balanced state with no change, is the standard meaning of inactivity here.

clue.text: Family overrun by moles beginning to show irritability

indicators.note: overrun by means the family word is surrounded by the moles word

parts.note: a mole is a spy inside an organisation
kin means one's relatives

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of show

explanation.surface: A family whose garden is overrun by moles starts to get tetchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Prickliness of temper, being easily annoyed, is the figurative sense of having spikes.

clue.text: At the front, painted orange and blue like some hotels

indicators.note: At the front means the opening letters of painted and orange

parts.note: blue means sad or downcast
as means like, in comparisons

explanation.surface: Some hotels are painted orange and blue on the facade.
explanation.definitionFit: A posada is a Spanish inn, so the plural names a kind of hotel.

clue.text: Drooling as girlfriend turns up with showy jewellery

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: bird is British slang for a girlfriend
bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Someone drools as a girlfriend arrives wearing flashy jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting saliva run from the mouth is the literal meaning, a synonym of drooling.

clue.text: Crazy way to spoil ceramist's work?

definitions.meaning: read literally, the answer split in two describes breaking a potter's vessel

explanation.surface: A wacky way to ruin a potter's creation.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild-eyed eccentric person is called by this informal term, so it works for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Engineers in railwaymen's union sent round for more fluid

indicators.note: sent round means the whole string is turned to read backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps
NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen in Britain

explanation.surface: Engineers within the rail union are sent elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flowing more freely, thinner in consistency, is the comparative of a liquid-like adjective.

clue.text: Emulate orphan lacking one new hat

indicators.note: lacking one means just one of the two N letters is taken away

parts.note: to emulate the orphan Annie (of the musical) is to be Annie

explanation.surface: Copy an orphan by doing without a new hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Orphan Annie is the comic-strip and musical heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: A small close-fitting knitted cap is a kind of hat.

clue.text: Acid no help in rehabilition

indicators.note: in rehabilitation means being reformed, so the letters of no help are remade (the clue misspells the word)

explanation.surface: No help is available to someone in rehab for acid use.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbolic acid is the chemical compound also known by this name, a mild acid.

clue.text: Commanding officer cheers, reaching a former colony

parts.note: chin-chin is a toast, like cheers

explanation.surface: A commanding officer raises a toast on arriving at an old colony.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern part of Vietnam was once a French colonial territory under this name.

clue.text: Pro-Remain foreign banker?

parts.note: con is the opposite of pro, as in pros and cons
go is the opposite of remain (stay or go)

explanation.surface: A foreign banker in favour of Britain remaining in the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: Each half is replaced by its opposite. 'banker' is crossword-speak for a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something with banks, and this great African river flows abroad.

clue.text: A wood pile finally burning

parts.note: fir is a type of wood

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of pile

explanation.surface: A woodpile is at last on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaze or alight, on fire, is the meaning of this literary adjective.

clue.text: Time to leave English city that's disgusting

indicators.note: to leave means the time letter departs from the city

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England

explanation.surface: Time to quit an English city, which is revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation expresses contempt or disgust, exactly like saying that's disgusting.

clue.text: Pasta: a bit, you say

indicators.note: you say means the word as heard rather than as written

parts.note: a bit is an old British coin, as is a penny

explanation.surface: Pasta costs just a bit, you'd say.
explanation.definitionFit: The quill-shaped tubes are a well-known type of Italian pasta.

clue.text: I race round province showing lack of enthusiasm

indicators.note: round means the race word goes around the province

parts.note: a nation is a people or race
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: Someone racing round a province shows no enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhaustion from lack of nourishment, hence lethargy and want of vigour.

clue.text: Twist and Shout — a fairly big number

indicators.note: Twist means the letters of and Shout are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: The Beatles' Twist and Shout, described as quite a large number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a song, but it is a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten hundreds is a respectable but not enormous figure.

clue.text: Girl stalks mountain cat

indicators.note: stalks means the girl word follows behind the mountain word

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for mountain
gal is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl tracks a mountain cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic breed with leopard-like spots, also the name of a tiger, is a kind of cat.
